fight: Should a Linux HA agent transport telemetry/commands over MQTT discovery, or over HA's native websocket/mobile_app API?

side_a.position: MQTT discovery is the established, community-endorsed bidirectional channel for companion agents; LWT gives offline detection nothing else provides; halinuxcompanion is migrating TO MQTT precisely for last-will semantics.
claims: MQTT discovery is the established bidirectional channel for companion agents
ha-linux-agent's MQTT architecture (with last-will/availability topics) is the correct design choice — halinuxcompanion author migrating to MQTT for offline detection
MQTT is the load-bearing bidirectional transport for command execution in existing desktop companions (HASS.Agent)
an external MQTT client publishing discovery directly is the community-validated pattern (HA mqtt.publish service renders templates at publish time and breaks discovery payloads)

side_b.position: MQTT is an unnecessary point of failure for host metrics; route telemetry directly into storage (Telegraf→InfluxDB) or use HA's native API with long-lived tokens — no broker dependency, no discovery staleness.
claims: koying's counter-position: routing host metrics through MQTT before storage adds an unnecessary point of failure
routing agent telemetry through HA's state machine before storage loses data (tags/metadata); an agent should publish to a database directly
an MQTT-free native-HA-API architecture is a proven alternative (ha_desktop_companion, go-hass-agent's mobile_app registration)

evidence_quality_delta: Side A is empirical (multiple production agents, spec docs); side B is practitioner-argument + one production counter-example (go-hass-agent dual-transport). Note go-hass-agent itself straddles: native API for sensors, MQTT for controls.
scope_overlap: Partially scoped differently — side A argues the companion-agent use case (bidirectional control + availability); side B argues the metrics-pipeline use case (time-series fidelity). Both can be right in their own scope; the fork is real for ha-linux-agent because its kiosk control features need bidirectionality but its server sensors need fidelity.
decision_relevance: high — determines whether the improvement roadmap doubles down on MQTT (fix lifecycle, keep rumqttc) or re-architects

fight: Should a fleet-wide Linux agent run as a systemd --user service (with linger) or as a system service (root or capability-scoped)?

side_a.position: User service + linger: no root, natural D-Bus session access for desktop features, jupiter-os already ships this pattern (ConditionUser=io, users.users.io.linger), go-hass-agent refuses root entirely.
claims: user-scoped systemd services are a viable mechanism for running an agent without granting sudo
privilege on a Linux HA agent is per-capability, not per-root; a NixOS fleet agent needs a wrapper or per-feature capabilities
fleet-wide headless deployment of a user-scoped agent on NixOS requires explicit lingering configuration (users.users.<name>.linger, NixOS 23.11+)
go-hass-agent refuses root; uses per-feature file capabilities

side_b.position: System service: user services have a rebuild/restart gap (systemd user units don't restart on nixos-rebuild switch), can't order after system units, need linger per user on every host, and jupiter-os's sysfs-perms already chmods nodes for the agent — a system service with User=/AmbientCapabilities is the fleet-native answer.
claims: a fleet agent targeting every host should run as a system service (optionally with User=)
an agent running as a user service cannot order itself after system-level units — a structural constraint
user services as a fleet-deployment mechanism on NixOS have a rebuild/restart gap that system services don't
the user-manager lifecycle is the core obstacle to user-scoped agents surviving on headless hosts (9-year declarative-linger gap, closed only Oct 2023)

evidence_quality_delta: Side B has the stronger structural argument for SERVER hosts (ordering, lifecycle); side A has the stronger security/practical argument for DESKTOP hosts (session bus for notifications/niri). The evidence reconciles by host-class, not by winner.
scope_overlap: Genuine disagreement for the headless-server case; both right if scoped: user-service on desktops/kiosks (session bus needed), system-service on headless hosts (no session, needs ordering). ha-linux-agent currently ships user-service-only — the fork decides europa/callisto coverage.
decision_relevance: high — this IS the 'every host in jupiterOS' question

fight: Is retained MQTT discovery alone sufficient for restart resilience, or must the agent also republish on HA birth-message and reconnection?

side_a.position: Retained discovery alone suffices — HA reads retained configs on every startup; ESPHome defaults discovery_retain=true for exactly this; hand-built devices with retained configs survive HA restarts.
claims: retained config+state+availability is the mechanism that makes Z2M-grade restart resilience
discovery_retain defaults true so entities re-appear automatically on Home Assistant restart

side_b.position: Retained alone is insufficient at fleet scale — HA's own docs mandate subscribing to the birth message and re-sending discovery on it; retained-message replay can overflow broker queue limits (5374-entity case); HASS.Agent shipped the republish bug (#230); retained staleness creates undeletable ghost entities.
claims: the assumption that retained discovery alone is sufficient for restart resilience is refuted (availability topic must receive payload; broker queue limits silently drop retained replay)
HA docs: a device exposing MQTT discovery should subscribe to the Birth message and use it as the trigger to send the discovery payload
HASS.Agent 2.1.1 fixed 'MQTT autodiscovery messages were not republished after connection was lost and recovered' — the same bug class ha-linux-agent has today
entity cleanup needs deliberate empty-payload publishes or ghosts persist (telegraf2hassio undeletable-entities complaint)

evidence_quality_delta: Side B is decisively stronger: HA official documentation + a maintainer-commented root-cause thread + a production agent's changelog. Side A describes the simple case that works until it doesn't.
scope_overlap: Genuine disagreement on the same scope; side B subsumes side A (retain AND republish).
decision_relevance: high — this is the direct fix for the user's 'never reliable' complaint

fight: Given go-hass-agent v14.15.1 is already in nixpkgs and lnxlink is community-endorsed, should ha-linux-agent be improved at all — or replaced/deprecated in favour of an incumbent?

side_a.position: Adopt: a mature agent already covers the every-host ambition; packaging, sensors, and controls exist; ha-linux-agent's differentiation (launcher groups, kiosk session control, ZFS, headscale) is small against the maintenance burden of a custom agent.
claims: a mature agent already covers the every-host ambition the user has for ha-linux-agent, so the build-vs-adopt decision must be argued
the build-vs-adopt decision for ha-linux-agent must be argued against an already-packaged, actively-maintained alternative
community mindshare for Linux HA agents centres on lnxlink and go-hass-agent

side_b.position: Build (fix) ha-linux-agent: jupiterOS-native differentiation is real — declarative NixOS module integration (jupiter.services.haAgent), launcher mutual-exclusion groups for kiosk/gaming session switching, ZFS/headscale/jupiter-specific backends, MQTT-only single-device identity (no go-hass-agent split-brain between mobile_app and MQTT integrations), systemd unit control with scope awareness.
claims: ha-linux-agent's MQTT-only design avoids the split-brain device identity problem that even the most mature Linux agent (go-hass-agent: two HA integrations for one device) has
NixOS users already hand-roll packaging for HA Linux agents — a first-class NixOS module is an unmet need ha-linux-agent fills
differentiation should centre on jupiterOS-native fleet integration (declarative per-host config, systemd hardening) rather than capability existence
fleet scaling of incumbents is linear manual work per host; declarative per-host modules are the NixOS-native answer

evidence_quality_delta: Balanced fight. Side A is factual (the incumbents exist and are packaged); side B is architectural (specific unmet jupiterOS needs). The honest synthesis must name what ha-linux-agent genuinely has that go-hass-agent lacks (launcher groups, ZFS, kiosk session switching) and concede what it lacks (audio select, events, script sensors, GPU sensors, packaging maturity).
scope_overlap: Same scope, values-weighted disagreement (maintenance cost vs integration fit).
decision_relevance: high — the user asked to 'improve it', but the research must honestly test whether improvement beats adoption

fight: Should the agent poll its sensor/command sources on an interval (current design), or subscribe to event streams (D-Bus signals, udev, niri event stream, zed, smartd hooks)?

side_a.position: Polling is simpler, bounded, and adequate at 30s cadence; sysinfo is diff-based and wants exactly one long-lived instance polling; interval publishes double as heartbeat (expire_after).
claims: sysinfo's design matches a long-running daemon; keep one System instance and poll it
periodic state publishes + expire_after gives availability without extra machinery
poll-interval selection is a real design parameter for storage/system collectors

side_b.position: Event-driven where events exist: D-Bus systemd signals beat failed-unit polling (systemd_mon), niri's event-stream pushes complete state then incremental updates, zed beats zpool polling, smartd -M exec is the sanctioned disk-event bridge, udev uevents keep backlight state in sync with hotkeys.
claims: event-driven DBus subscription (mirroring zbus) is the correct architecture for unit-state monitoring — no polling, no busy-loops
a jupiterOS kiosk agent can consume compositor state via niri's event stream (complete state up-front then incremental updates) instead of polling niri msg
disk-failure alerting can be event-driven: smartd -M exec hooks are the sanctioned bridge
agent brightness state stays in sync with hotkey/firmware changes by listening for uevents

evidence_quality_delta: Both sides are correct in their own layer — the reconciliation is hybrid: poll cheap sysfs/procfs sensors, subscribe where kernel/D-Bus events exist. Side B's evidence is architectural-primary; side A's is operational.
scope_overlap: Scoped differently (sysfs scalar sensors vs stateful subsystems); both right — hybrid design.
decision_relevance: medium-high — shapes the sensor architecture for fleet scale and the watchdog story
